e) Have the capacity to receive funds via PayNow Corporate or bank transfer to a Singapore-based bank account.

Informal groups are strongly encouraged to approach a registered charity early in the application process to secure sponsorship. The Grants Operations Team can provide a list of potential sponsoring organisations upon request.

3. PRIORITY AREAS FOR 2025

While all eligible proposals will be considered, the following themes have been identified as priority areas for this cycle:

- Digital inclusion for seniors and low-income households
- Mental wellness and peer support networks
- Environmental sustainability at the neighbourhood level (e.g., community gardens, recycling initiatives)
- Befriending and outreach programmes for isolated residents
- Youth-led community action projects

Proposals that incorporate volunteer management training or include a clear sustainability plan beyond the grant period will be viewed favourably.

4. WHAT THE GRANT COVERS

COP funding may be used for:

- Project coordination and manpower costs (up to 30% of total budget)
- Venue rental and equipment
- Materials and supplies
- Publicity and outreach
- Professional fees (e.g., trainers, facilitators, counsellors)
- Evaluation and reporting costs
- Miscellaneous expenses (up to 5% of total budget)

The Community Outreach Programme (COP) announcement sets application_deadline 2025-03-31. Record status: historical.

The following are NOT covered:

- Capital expenditure exceeding $10,000 (e.g., renovation of premises)
- Recurring overheads not directly attributable to the project
- Overseas travel
- Gifts, vouchers, or cash incentives for participants (except for token appreciation items valued at $10 or less per participant)
- Fundraising expenses that are not part of the project’s core activities

Applicants are advised to budget carefully. The Grants Operations Team reserves the right to disallow any budget line item that is not clearly justified.

5. APPLICATION PROCEDURE

Step 1: Download the COP 2025 Application Form and Budget Template from our website (www.grants.gov.sg/cop2025).

Step 2: Complete the application form. Ensure that all sections are filled in, including the project logic model, risk assessment, and monitoring plan.

Step 3: Prepare the following supporting documents:
   - A copy of the organisation’s latest annual report or equivalent (if applicable)
   - A copy of the organisation’s constitution or rules
   - A copy of the latest financial statements or audited accounts (if applicable)
   - A letter of sponsorship from the sponsoring charity (for informal groups only)
   - NRIC or FIN numbers of all key personnel (for background screening purposes)
   - A detailed project timeline (include milestones and key deliverables)

Step 4: Submit the completed application via the online portal at https://grants.gov.sg/portal. Do NOT email your application unless you have received prior approval from the Grants Operations Team.

Step 5: Applications will be acknowledged within 5 working days of receipt. If you do not receive an acknowledgement, please contact us at cop@nvpc.org.sg.

6. EVALUATION PROCESS

**7. EVALUATION PROCESS**

All complete applications received by the deadline will be assessed in two stages.

**Stage 1: Eligibility Screening (1 – 8 April 2025)**
Applications will be checked against the eligibility criteria set out in Section 2 of this announcement. Incomplete applications, or those that do not meet the basic eligibility requirements, will be disqualified at this stage. Applicants will be notified of disqualification by 11 April 2025.

**Stage 2: Merit Assessment (14 April – 23 May 2025)**
Eligible applications will be assessed by a Review Panel comprising representatives from the National Volunteer & Philanthropy Centre (NVPC), relevant government agencies, and community partners.

The Review Panel will evaluate applications based on the following criteria:

| Criterion | Weightage | What We Look For |
|-----------|-----------|------------------|
| Alignment with COP objectives | 25% | How well the project addresses a clear community need and contributes to the outcomes of the COP |
| Project design & feasibility | 25% | Clarity of project logic model, realistic timeline, and sound methodology |
| Organisational capacity | 20% | Track record, governance, and ability to deliver the project |
| Value for money | 15% | Reasonableness of budget relative to projected outcomes |
| Sustainability & impact | 15% | Plans for sustaining benefits beyond the grant period, and potential for long-term community impact |

*Note: The weightages above were revised from the draft version circulated in January 2025. The earlier draft had weighted "Project design & feasibility" at 30% and "Sustainability & impact" at 10%. The final weightages reflect feedback from the 2024 grant cycle review.*

**Interviews / Site Visits**
Shortlisted applicants may be invited for an interview or a site visit between 5 May and 16 May 2025. Not all shortlisted applicants will be interviewed; the Review Panel will determine the need for further clarification on a case-by-case basis.

**8. NOTIFICATION OF OUTCOMES**

All applicants will be notified of the outcome of their application by **30 June 2025** via the email address provided in the application form.

- **Successful applicants** will receive a Grant Offer Letter, which must be accepted and returned within **14 working days** of the date of the letter.
- **Unsuccessful applicants** will receive brief feedback on why their application was not successful, to support future applications.

Successful applicants must comply with the following conditions:

**10. FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (FAQs)**

**Q1: Can my organisation submit more than one application under COP 2025?**
No. Each organisation may submit only one application per grant cycle. If you wish to propose multiple projects, please contact the Grants Operations Team to discuss which project is most suitable for COP.

**Q2: We are an informal group. Do we need to be registered with ROS or an equivalent body to apply?**
No, informal groups may apply, provided they have a sponsoring charity. Please refer to Section 2 of this announcement for the full eligibility criteria. The sponsoring charity must be a registered organisation and must submit a letter of sponsorship as part of the application.

**Q3: Can we include GST in our budget?**
Yes, GST is an allowable cost. For organisations that are GST-registered, please indicate the GST component separately in the Budget Template. For organisations that are not GST-registered, please include GST as part of the item cost.

While all eligible proposals will be considered, the following themes have been identified as priority areas for this cycle:

**7. EVALUATION PROCESS**

All complete applications received by the deadline will be assessed in two stages.

**Stage 1: Eligibility Screening (1 – 8 April 2025)**
Applications will be checked against the eligibility criteria set out in Section 2 of this announcement. Incomplete applications, or those that do not meet the basic eligibility requirements, will be disqualified at this stage. Applicants will be notified of disqualification by 11 April 2025.

**Stage 2: Merit Assessment (14 April – 23 May 2025)**
Eligible applications will be assessed by a Review Panel comprising representatives from the National Volunteer & Philanthropy Centre (NVPC), relevant government agencies, and community partners.

The Review Panel will evaluate applications based on the following criteria:

| Criterion | Weightage | What We Look For |
|-----------|-----------|------------------|
| Alignment with COP objectives | 25% | How well the project addresses a clear community need and contributes to the outcomes of the COP |
| Project design & feasibility | 25% | Clarity of project logic model, realistic timeline, and sound methodology |
| Organisational capacity | 20% | Track record, governance, and ability to deliver the project |
| Value for money | 15% | Reasonableness of budget relative to projected outcomes |
| Sustainability & impact | 15% | Plans for sustaining benefits beyond the grant period, and potential for long-term community impact |

*Note: The weightages above were revised from the draft version circulated in January 2025. The earlier draft had weighted "Project design & feasibility" at 30% and "Sustainability & impact" at 10%. The final weightages reflect feedback from the 2024 grant cycle review.*

**Interviews / Site Visits**
Shortlisted applicants may be invited for an interview or a site visit between 5 May and 16 May 2025. Not all shortlisted applicants will be interviewed; the Review Panel will determine the need for further clarification on a case-by-case basis.

**8. NOTIFICATION OF OUTCOMES**

All applicants will be notified of the outcome of their application by **30 June 2025** via the email address provided in the application form.

- **Successful applicants** will receive a Grant Offer Letter, which must be accepted and returned within **14 working days** of the date of the letter.
- **Unsuccessful applicants** will receive brief feedback on why their application was not successful, to support future applications.

**10. FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (FAQs)**

**Q1: Can my organisation submit more than one application under COP 2025?**
No. Each organisation may submit only one application per grant cycle. If you wish to propose multiple projects, please contact the Grants Operations Team to discuss which project is most suitable for COP.

**Q2: We are an informal group. Do we need to be registered with ROS or an equivalent body to apply?**
No, informal groups may apply, provided they have a sponsoring charity. Please refer to Section 2 of this announcement for the full eligibility criteria. The sponsoring charity must be a registered organisation and must submit a letter of sponsorship as part of the application.

**Q3: Can we include GST in our budget?**
Yes, GST is an allowable cost. For organisations that are GST-registered, please indicate the GST component separately in the Budget Template. For organisations that are not GST-registered, please include GST as part of the item cost.

9.1 The Fund may conduct site visits, interviews, or surveys to monitor the implementation of the Programme. The Grantee shall facilitate such monitoring activities and provide access to relevant documents and personnel.

9.2 The Fund may engage an independent evaluator to assess the Programme's outcomes. The Grantee shall cooperate fully with such evaluation, including providing participant contact details (subject to consent) and programme data.

9.3 The Grantee shall participate in any learning or sharing sessions organised by the Fund, where reasonable, to share lessons from the Programme with other grantees.

---

10.1 Any variation to this Agreement, including the budget lines in Annex B, shall be made in writing and signed by both parties. The Grantee may request a variation by submitting a written proposal to the Fund, including justification and revised budget details.

(a) the Grantee commits a material breach of any term of this Agreement and fails to remedy such breach within thirty (30) days of receiving written notice;

If the dispute is not resolved by mediation within sixty (60) days, either party may refer the matter to the courts of Singapore.

---

**12. NOTICES**

12.1 All notices and communications under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed duly given if delivered by hand, sent by registered post, or transmitted by email to the addresses set out in Annex E.

(c) a final financial report and statement of account within ninety (90) days after the end of the Project Period, certified by the Grantee's auditor or an independent accountant acceptable to the Fund.

Notwithstanding the above, the Fund may require more frequent reporting if, in its reasonable opinion, there is a material variance between actual and budgeted expenditure.

Any unexpended portion of the payments made under Section C.2 shall be returned to the Fund within sixty (60) days after the end of the Project Period, or within thirty (30) days of the Fund's written request, whichever is earlier.
